pli-tv-bu-vb-np9:1.39: The phrase ubhova santā ekena, here translated as “put together”, is not immediately clear. It seems to me that this phrase needs to be related to the main sentence verb acchādetha, “present” or “give”, which takes the instrumental of the thing given: “present (him) with one (robe)”. Ubhova santā is explained below in the word analysis as dvepi janā, “both people”, and the overall phrase then becomes, “two people present (him) with one (robe)”. This means that the funds are put together, and I translate accordingly.
pli-tv-bu-vb-np9:2.6: For an explanation of this, see comment at Bu NP 4:2.1.6.
pli-tv-bu-vb-np9:2.8: Agāraṁ is typically rendered as “in a house”. The problem with this is that it is not unallowable for a monastic to live in a building that is the equivalent of a house. What a monastic should not do is own a home and then live there.
